method: Page fetched directly with curl and converted from HTML to text. Every claim is verbatim-checked against that file with scripts/verify.py. Prose paraphrases; source_text stays verbatim. The fingertip-unit table is transcribed from the page's text rendering of the table, so the row values are checked as fragments rather than as a reconstructed grid -- a person should confirm the grid alignment against the page before clinical use. No antibiotic or antiviral agent or dose appears in the source and none is reconstructed.

claims.claim: Eczema affects 30% of children and often develops before 12 months
claims.source_text: Eczema affects 30% of children, and often develops before 12 months of age. Some children develop lifelong eczema

claims.claim: No requirement to use steroids sparingly or take breaks
claims.source_text: There is no requirement to use steroids 'sparingly' or for regular breaks from steroids during treatment for eczema flares. Steroids should be applied generously followed by moisturiser

claims.claim: Topical steroids do not cause the commonly feared harms when used as directed
claims.source_text: Topical steroids do not cause atrophy, hypopigmentation, hypertrichosis, osteoporosis, purpura or telangiectasia when used as per guidelines. Rare complications such as striae, adrenal suppression and ophthalmological disease have been reported with prolonged and excessive use of potent topical steroids

claims.claim: Topical steroids are safe, effective and essential for flares
claims.source_text: Topical steroids are safe and effective when used correctly, and are essential to the treatment of eczema flares

claims.claim: Steroids can be applied to broken and infected skin
claims.source_text: They can be applied to broken and infected skin

claims.claim: Everyday skin management is required regardless of skin appearance
claims.source_text: Children with eczema require optimal everyday skin management regardless of the appearance of their skin

claims.claim: Fingertip Unit method is used for dosing
claims.source_text: Steroid cream dosage for application be calculated using the … Fingertip Unit " method

claims.claim: The fingertip unit table gives units per body area for five age bands
claims.source_text: Fingertip Units per body area Face and neck Arm and hand Leg and foot Anterior chest and abdomen Back and buttocks 3-12 months 1 1 1 ½ 1 1 ½ >1-3 years 1 ½ 1 ½ 2 2 3 >3-6 years 1 ½ 2 3 3 3 ½ >6-10 years 2 2 ½ 4 ½ 3 ½ 5 >10 years 2 ½ 4 8 8 7

claims.claim: Steroids applied once or twice daily until skin is completely clear
claims.source_text: Topical steroids (see additional resources below) are required once or twice daily until the skin is completely clear to reduce skin inflammation

claims.claim: Hydrocortisone 1% for sensitive areas in mild to moderate flare
claims.source_text: Mild to moderate flare: Use mild potency steroid eg Hydrocortisone 1% ointment or cream

claims.claim: Methylprednisolone aceponate for severe sensitive-area flare with duration limits
claims.source_text: Severe flare: Use moderate potency steroid eg Methylprednisolone aceponate 0.1% ointment or cream for short term use only, max 3-5 days on face/neck, 7-14 days on groin

claims.claim: Body flare agents by severity
claims.source_text: Mild to moderate flare: Use moderate potency steroid eg Methylprednisolone aceponate 0.1% fatty ointment, ointment or cream … Severe flare: Use potent steroid eg Mometasone furoate 0.1% ointment or cream

claims.claim: Very potent steroids need dermatological advice
claims.source_text: Very potent topical steroids eg Betamethasone dipropionate 0.05% should not be used without dermatological advice

claims.claim: Application frequency by agent
claims.source_text: Hydrocortisone: Apply twice a day until symptoms resolved … Mometasone and methylprednisolone: Apply once a day until symptoms resolved

claims.claim: Ointments preferred; lotions for hairy areas
claims.source_text: Ointments are preferred to creams for their emollient effects … Lotions are best used for hairy areas eg scalp

claims.claim: Pimecrolimus 1% second line over 3 months with course limits
claims.source_text: Mild to moderate flare: Pimecrolimus 1% cream can be used as second-line treatment in children >3 months … Treatment courses should be limited to 6 weeks (3 weeks if 3-23 months age)

claims.claim: Low potency steroids for mild to moderate facial eczema
claims.source_text: Mild to moderate facial eczema should be treated with low potency steroids to avoid chemical skin irritation

claims.claim: Moisturiser application and type
claims.source_text: Apply moisturisers generously top-to-toe twice per day, including after bathing … A thick, plain moisturising cream, with high oil and low water content should be used

claims.claim: Moisturiser ingredients to avoid
claims.source_text: Avoid moisturisers containing fragrance, alcohol, sodium lauryl sulfate, plant or food products (eg cow or goat milk, vegetable, nut or olive oils) as these may disrupt the skin barrier and sensitise the skin

claims.claim: Avoid contaminating the moisturiser
claims.source_text: Avoid contaminating the moisturiser with bacteria from the hands. Use a spatula or spoon to remove cream from tub

claims.claim: Daily bathing reduces bacterial load; keep baths under 31 degrees
claims.source_text: Daily bathing (where water quality/access allows) aids to reduce the bacterial skin load and reduce the risk of infection … Baths and showers should be kept luke-warm (<31°C)

claims.claim: No soap or shampoo
claims.source_text: Do not use soap or shampoo. Use soap-free skin cleansers that will not irritate the skin

claims.claim: Bath oil increases slipping risk and needs supervision
claims.source_text: A capful of bath oil may be added to bath water, advise parents this increases risk of child slipping, and direct supervision is always required

claims.claim: Named contact sensitisers to avoid
claims.source_text: Avoid wash/cleanser products or hair washing products that contain methylisothiazolinone (MI) or methylchloroisothiazolinone (MCI) and nappy wipes that contain benzalkonium chloride, as these can cause contact dermatitis

claims.claim: Moisturiser goes on top of topical medicines
claims.source_text: Apply the moisturiser on top of other topical medicines such as steroids

claims.claim: Allergy testing usually not required and restrictive diets usually unhelpful
claims.source_text: Allergy testing is usually not required. Restrictive diets are usually not helpful, and parents should seek advice from a dermatologist or general paediatrician before eliminating foods from the diet

claims.claim: Non-sedating antihistamines do not improve eczema itch
claims.source_text: Non-sedating antihistamines do not improve eczema itch, but may be considered if there is concomitant urticaria or allergic rhinitis

claims.claim: Common reasons treatment fails
claims.source_text: Inadequate education regarding eczema and the correct use of eczema treatments … Inadequate application of moisturisers, topical steroids and/or wet dressings … Ongoing exposure to eczema triggers … Inability to identify and treat skin infections … MRSA bacterial infection

claims.claim: Flares commonly due to inadequate education and triggers
claims.source_text: Eczema flares are commonly due to inadequate caregiver education on eczema management, and triggers such as skin infection, irritant exposure and heat

claims.claim: All children should get a home eczema management plan
claims.source_text: All children with eczema should be provided with a home eczema management plan, including steps to manage an eczema flare

claims.claim: Wet dressings purpose and frequency
claims.source_text: Wet dressings assist to return moisture to the skin, protect from infection and further trauma, and help to reduce irritation and itch … Dressings should be applied with every flare 1-4 times daily for at least 3 days … May be used in eczematous skin infections, in addition to antimicrobial treatment

claims.claim: Cool compresses for facial itch
claims.source_text: Cool compresses (cloth or towel soaked in water and/or bath oil) can used on the face to provide immediate relief of itch

claims.claim: Bleach bath method
claims.source_text: Bleach baths can be used daily with every flare to reduce the bacterial skin load … The child's face and head should be wet during the bath, but not submerged

claims.claim: Distribution by age
claims.source_text: the cheeks, scalp and extensor surfaces are most often affected … In older children, eczema commonly presents as flexural dermatitis eg antecubital fossae, popliteal fossae, neck, front of ankles, periorbital area

claims.claim: Severity definitions
claims.source_text: Normal skin, no evidence of active atopic eczema … Areas of dry skin, infrequent itching (with or without small areas of redness) … Areas of dry skin, frequent itching, redness (with or without excoriation and localised skin thickening) … Widespread areas of dry skin, incessant itching, redness (with or without excoriation, extensive skin thickening, bleeding, oozing, cracking and alteration of pigmentation)

claims.claim: Features of infected eczema
claims.source_text: Cutaneous features include increasing itch, crusted, vesicular, satellite, pustular, erosive, tender, scabbed or weeping lesions on eczematous skin … Systemic features include fever and malaise

claims.claim: Appearance of bacterial, herpetic and coxsackie infection
claims.source_text: Itchy yellowish crusts, weeping, pustules, folliculitis … Painful clustered blisters, punched-out erosions … Vesiculobullous rash with brownish discolouration, satellite lesions surrounding areas of dermatitis

claims.claim: New itchy rash in multiple family members suggests scabies
claims.source_text: New itchy rash affecting multiple family members (consider scabies)

claims.claim: Broken skin carries high infection risk with named organisms
claims.source_text: Broken eczematous skin has a high-risk of bacterial and/or viral skin infections … Common causative organisms include Staphylococcus aureus (consider MRSA in high-risk groups or if not responding to first-line antibiotics) and Streptococcus pyogenes

claims.claim: Remove crusts before applying steroids and moisturisers
claims.source_text: Remove crusted lesions by wiping them gently with a cloth whilst soaking in the bath. Only apply topical steroids and moisturisers after the crusts are removed

claims.claim: Systemic or severe infection may need admission and IV antibiotics
claims.source_text: Children who have systemic features or severe infections may require admission and intravenous antibiotics

claims.claim: Viral infection often coexists with bacterial infection
claims.source_text: Often co-exist with bacterial infection, consider if infected eczema is not responding to antibiotic management

claims.claim: Eczema herpeticum needs prompt antivirals and urgent ophthalmology if periorbital
claims.source_text: Herpes simplex infection (eczema herpeticum) requires prompt initiation of antiviral treatment. Intravenous antiviral treatment may be required in severe infections. Urgent Ophthalmology review is required if the infection affects the periorbital area

claims.claim: Decolonisation and antiseptics for recurrent infection
claims.source_text: Staphylococcus aureus decolonisation … Antiseptic preparations may reduce skin bacterial load eg bleach baths, triclosan skin cleanser, chlorhexidine skin wash

claims.claim: Paediatric consultation triggers
claims.source_text: Eczema herpeticum or severe bacterial eczematous skin infections … Moderate or severe eczema not responding to treatment despite compliance with correct treatment for 2 weeks or more … Concern that the child's carers are not able to provide appropriate eczema treatments and are unable to access outpatient supports … Poor feeding, poor sleep, failure to thrive … Suspicion of systemic disease eg immunodeficiency or micronutrient deficiency

claims.claim: Dermatology referral for chronic uncontrolled eczema
claims.source_text: Chronic eczema not controlled with optimised topical therapies and everyday skin management, for consideration of systemic therapies

claims.claim: Prescribe multiple quantities and repeats
claims.source_text: Provide children with prescriptions for multiple quantities and repeats (PBS authority where applicable) of each medication

claims.claim: Tests are not usually required
claims.source_text: Tests are not usually required

claims.claim: Discoid eczema is persistent and treatment resistant
claims.source_text: Associated with increased persistence and treatment resistance, often requiring extended treatment courses with potent steroids
